materials.detail: Pumice powder (PP) was an industrial by-product produced by Hebei Runhuabang New Materials Technology Co., Ltd., (Shijiazhuang, China).

materials.name: RFA
materials.detail: The apparent density, water absorption, and fineness modulus of the RFA were 2273 kg/m3, 9.4%, and 2.9, respectively.

materials.name: NaOH
materials.detail: The NaOH solution had a concentration of 10 mol/L and was prepared 24 h before mixing and allowed to cool to room temperature.

materials.name: Na2SiO3
materials.detail: The sodium silicate solution contained 21.5 wt.% SiO2, 18.5 wt.% Na2O, and 60 wt.% H2O, corresponding to a silica modulus (Ms = SiO2/Na2O molar ratio) of 1.2.

cures.text: After casting, the specimens were sealed and cured at 70 °C for 24 h. They were subsequently demoulded and stored under standard curing conditions (20 ± 2 °C, RH ≥ 95%) until an age of 7 days.

results.text: PP70 exhibited the highest compressive strength (31.7 MPa) among the PP-containing mixtures, exceeding that of PP60 (30.1 MPa) by 5.3% and remaining only 1.6% lower than that of PP0 (32.2 MPa).

findings.text: PP70 exhibited the highest compressive strength (31.7 MPa) among the PP-containing mixtures, exceeding that of PP60 (30.1 MPa) by 5.3% and remaining only 1.6% lower than that of PP0 (32.2 MPa).

gaps: Table quotes follow the standard form; "PP" is pumice powder (not polypropylene) and replaces RFA by equal absolute volume. NaOH is the 10 mol/L solution as dosed.

Ambient values were tested at 7 days after the same 50 °C drying as the heated specimens. Residual values exist for 600–800 °C and 1 or 3 h holds; only those whose sentences name the 800 °C / 3 h condition are transcribed. The PP70 1 h versus 3 h series (30.7→28.2 MPa at 600 °C; 25.0→18.8 MPa at 800 °C; bond 2.4→2.0, 2.2→1.5, 1.9→1.1 MPa) is left in the paper.
Table 5 carbon intensity is embodied carbon divided by strength; strengths are not back-calculated from it.
